questions.explain: A U.S.-led coalition, joined by the UK, Australia and Poland, invaded on March 20, 2003.

questions.q: What was a stated justification for the 2003 invasion of Iraq that was not borne out afterward?
options: That Iraq had invaded Saudi Arabia
That Iraq had attacked Israel directly
That Iraq possessed long-range ballistic missiles that could reach the U.S. mainland
That Iraq possessed weapons of mass destruction
questions.explain: No stockpiles of weapons of mass destruction were found, and the 9/11 Commission found no credible evidence linking Saddam to al-Qaeda.

questions.q: What was the 2007 U.S. troop surge in Iraq meant to do?
options: Stabilize parts of Iraq amid sectarian violence
Begin the withdrawal of all troops
questions.explain: The 2007 surge added about 20,000 or more combat troops, and violence fell in many areas of Iraq in 2007 and 2008.

questions.q: In what year did the last U.S. troops leave Iraq under the 2008 security agreement?
questions.explain: The last U.S. troops left Iraq in December 2011, during President Obama's first term.

questions.q: Which dictator was captured in 2003 and executed in 2006?
questions.explain: U.S. forces captured Saddam Hussein near Tikrit in December 2003. An Iraqi court convicted him of crimes against humanity, and he was executed in December 2006.

questions.q: Why did the Soviet Union not veto the UN Security Council resolutions on Korea in June 1950?
options: It had already declared war on North Korea
Its ambassador had been recalled after a spy scandal
It was boycotting the Council over China's seat
questions.explain: The Soviets had boycotted since January 1950 to protest that the Republic of China, not the People's Republic, held China's seat.

questions.q: How did the UN Security Council vote on Resolution 83 on June 27, 1950, recommending aid to South Korea?
questions.explain: The council found the North Korean attack a breach of the peace. Yugoslavia voted no, Egypt and India abstained, and the Soviet seat was empty.

questions.q: Why did Truman call the Korean conflict a "police action"?
options: Congress had voted a limited declaration
The war took place only inside South Korea
It was fought only by the police forces of the allies
The U.S. never formally declared war and acted under the UN flag
questions.explain: Truman used the phrase because the United States never formally declared war and acted under the UN flag.

questions.q: Who selected the 38th parallel as the dividing line in Korea on August 11, 1945?
options: General Douglas MacArthur and General Omar Bradley
President Truman and Stalin at Potsdam
U.S. Colonels Dean Rusk and Charles Bonesteel
Secretary of State James Byrnes alone
questions.explain: Dean Rusk and Charles H. Bonesteel III chose the line as the Soviets entered northern Korea and the U.S. prepared to occupy the south.

questions.q: Which political leader was elected president of South Korea in July 1948, shortly before the Republic of Korea was proclaimed on August 15?
questions.explain: The Republic of Korea was established on August 15, 1948, with Syngman Rhee as president.

questions.q: Which forces withdrew from Korea in 1948 and 1949, before the war began?
options: British troops in 1948 and Japanese troops in 1949
Soviet troops in 1948 and American troops in 1949
Chinese troops in 1948 and Soviet troops in 1949
American troops in 1948 and Soviet troops in 1949
questions.explain: The Soviets withdrew from the north in 1948 and the Americans left the south in 1949, a year before the invasion.

questions.q: When did Chinese forces cross the Yalu River and enter the Korean War?
questions.explain: The Chinese People's Volunteer Army crossed the Yalu on October 19, 1950.

questions.q: Which river formed the border between North Korea and China and was crossed by Chinese forces in October 1950?
questions.explain: Chinese forces crossed the Yalu in October 1950 as UN forces approached the border.

questions.q: According to the UN Command, about what share of its ground troops were South Korean when its strength peaked in 1952?
questions.explain: The UN Command says that at its 1952 peak about 50 percent of its ground troops were South Korean, 40 percent American and 10 percent from other member nations.

questions.q: Which British battalion was cut off and surrounded on Hill 235 at the Imjin River in April 1951?
questions.explain: The Glosters were cut off and surrounded on April 22-25, 1951, slowing the Chinese offensive.

questions.q: The Imjin River battle in April 1951 was part of which Chinese operation?
questions.explain: The Chinese aimed to break through and recapture Seoul in the spring offensive of April 1951.

questions.q: Who signed Executive Order 9981 on July 26, 1948, ending discrimination in the armed forces?
questions.explain: Truman's order called for equality of treatment and opportunity in the armed services. Integration took several years and was largely complete by the mid-1950s.

questions.q: What did Executive Order 9981 do?
options: Ended racial discrimination in the armed forces
questions.explain: Truman signed it on July 26, 1948, and it set a policy of equal treatment and opportunity in the armed services.

questions.q: Which Supreme Court case in 1952 held that Truman could not seize the nation's steel mills during the Korean War?
options: Youngstown Sheet & Tube Co. v. Sawyer
questions.explain: The Court ruled 6-3 on June 2, 1952, that the president lacked authority to seize the mills.

questions.q: By what vote did the Supreme Court decide Youngstown Sheet & Tube Co. v. Sawyer in June 1952?
questions.explain: Justice Black wrote the majority opinion. Chief Justice Vinson and Justices Reed and Minton dissented.

questions.q: Which justice's concurrence in the steel seizure case set out three categories of presidential power?
questions.explain: Jackson's three categories depend on whether the president acts with, without or against the will of Congress.

questions.q: What did Truman do when the strike in the steel industry threatened defense production in April 1952?
options: He invoked the draft against strikers
He asked Congress for a declaration of war
He shut down the mills for a month
questions.explain: He believed a strike would hurt defense production and kept management running the mills under federal direction.

questions.q: Who was the first African American naval officer killed in the Korean War?
questions.explain: Brown's Corsair was hit on December 4, 1950, during the Chosin Reservoir battle. Wingman Thomas Hudner crash-landed to try to save him and received the Medal of Honor.

questions.q: Which wingman received the Medal of Honor for trying to rescue Jesse Brown near the Chosin Reservoir?
questions.explain: Hudner crash-landed nearby and tried to save Brown, who died of his injuries and exposure.

questions.q: Which prisoner exchange of August 1953 returned captured American and allied soldiers after the armistice?
questions.explain: Big Switch began August 5, 1953, at Panmunjom, with 3,597 Americans among those returned.

questions.q: What was Operation Little Switch, April 20 to May 3, 1953?
options: An early exchange of sick and wounded prisoners
The airlift of Americans from Hungnam
A Chinese attack on Pork Chop Hill
questions.explain: The Little Switch exchange returned 684 UN soldiers, including 149 Americans, and 6,670 communist prisoners and civilian internees.

questions.q: About how many communist prisoners refused repatriation and were handed to a neutral commission in September 1953?
questions.explain: On September 23, 1953, 22,604 communist soldiers who refused repatriation were handed to the Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission.

questions.q: Where was the 1951 battle of Heartbreak Ridge fought?
options: In the mountains of central Korea north of the 38th parallel
questions.explain: The battle ran from September 13 to October 15, 1951, in the mountains north of the 38th parallel, fought by the 2nd Infantry Division and attached French and Dutch battalions.

questions.q: Which French battalion stormed Hill 851 at Heartbreak Ridge on October 13, 1951?
options: The French Battalion attached to the U.S. 2nd Infantry Division
The French Foreign Legion from Algeria
questions.explain: The French Battalion's attack on October 13, 1951, gave the U.S. control of the ridge.

questions.q: What name did UN pilots give to the northwestern part of North Korea where jet fighters fought in the Korean War?
questions.explain: The first large-scale jet-versus-jet battles took place there between Soviet-built MiG-15s and F-86 Sabres.

questions.q: Which American fighter jet mainly fought the MiG-15 in MiG Alley?
questions.explain: The F-86 Sabre met the MiG-15 in the first large jet-versus-jet air battles and helped UN forces gain the upper hand in the air.

questions.q: What secret did the Soviet Union keep for decades about the air war in Korea?
options: Soviet airmen flew MiGs in disguise against UN planes
questions.explain: Soviet airmen flew MiGs starting in November 1950 but the Soviet Union never officially entered the war.

questions.q: Which U.S. Air Force ace claimed 16 MiG kills in the Korean War?
questions.explain: McConnell is cited as the leading UN ace, with 16 claimed kills.

questions.q: What name is given to April 12, 1951, when MiG-15s shot down several B-29 bombers over northwest Korea?
questions.explain: After the losses on April 12, 1951, B-29 missions over the Sinuiju area were halted for about three months until more F-86 Sabres arrived.

questions.q: Which city did North Korea capture on June 28, 1950, three days into the war?
questions.explain: North Korean forces captured Seoul, South Korea's capital, on June 28, 1950. UN forces retook the city that September after the landing at Inchon.

questions.q: What did the 1953 armistice do to the territory around the 38th parallel?
options: Moved the line so South Korea gained Sokcho and North Korea gained Kaesong
Gave all of Seoul to the north
Made the Yalu River the border
questions.explain: The new line followed where the armies stood when fighting stopped, so South Korea gained land in the east, including Sokcho, while North Korea gained Kaesong in the west.

questions.q: What is the Joint Security Area at Panmunjom?
options: An American air base near Seoul
A prison camp for prisoners of war
A United Nations headquarters in Pusan
The meeting site on the DMZ created by the armistice
questions.explain: The armistice created a 4-km DMZ with a Joint Security Area at Panmunjom, where armistice talks were held.

questions.q: Who gave initial approval on January 30, 1950, to Kim Il Sung's preparations for war?
questions.explain: Stalin approved the preparations in January and let Kim attack in April on the condition that Mao would send reinforcements if needed.

questions.q: What was the first draft lottery, held on December 1, 1969, designed to do?
options: Choose draftees by random birth-date order instead of local board decisions
questions.explain: The lottery added a random element to reduce bias in selection. The first date drawn, September 14, got number 1.

questions.q: Which birth date received lottery number 1 in the December 1, 1969, draft lottery?
questions.explain: Men born from 1944 through 1950 were included in the first drawing, and September 14 was drawn first.

questions.q: When was the last man drafted into the U.S. Army during the Vietnam era?
questions.explain: More than 1.7 million men were drafted between 1965 and 1973.

questions.q: How quickly was the Twenty-sixth Amendment ratified after being proposed in 1971?
options: In about 100 days, the fastest of any amendment
questions.explain: It was proposed on March 23, 1971, and ratified in about 100 days.

questions.q: What did the Supreme Court decide in Oregon v. Mitchell (1970) about the voting age of 18?
options: It could be set by Congress for state but not federal elections
It was unconstitutional for all elections
It could never be changed by Congress
It could be set by Congress for federal but not state elections
questions.explain: That ruling left states needing separate voter rolls, so Congress proposed the Twenty-sixth Amendment.

questions.q: What was notable about the Battle of Ia Drang in November 1965?
options: It was the last battle of the war
It was fought entirely by Marines
It was the first major battle between U.S. Army and North Vietnamese regulars
It took place in the Mekong Delta
questions.explain: The battle, November 14-18, 1965, was also the first large-scale helicopter air assault.

questions.q: Which lieutenant colonel led the 1st Battalion, 7th Cavalry at LZ X-Ray in the Ia Drang battle?
questions.explain: Moore's battalion was surrounded at LZ X-Ray but held for three days with air and artillery support.

questions.q: Which unit used helicopters to fight at Ia Drang in November 1965?
questions.explain: The 1st Cavalry Division, testing air mobility tactics, relied on helicopters, artillery and close air support.

questions.q: What was Operation Linebacker II, which took place in December 1972?
options: A ground invasion of North Vietnam
A heavy bombing campaign against Hanoi and Haiphong, also called the Christmas bombing
A U.S. naval blockade of Haiphong harbor
questions.explain: It ran from December 18 to 29, 1972, after the Paris peace talks stalled in mid-December.

questions.q: Which aircraft did the U.S. use most prominently in Linebacker II?
questions.explain: B-52 bombers flew hundreds of sorties from Guam and Thailand in the campaign, and several were shot down.

questions.q: What did North Vietnam agree to after Linebacker II ended?
options: To sign a mutual defense pact
To return to the peace talks in Paris
questions.explain: Bombing north of the 20th parallel was suspended on December 30, 1972, and the accords were signed January 27, 1973.

questions.q: On what date did South Vietnamese generals launch the coup against Diem, with tacit U.S. backing?
questions.explain: Diem and his brother Nhu escaped the palace but surrendered the next morning and were killed on November 2.

questions.q: What was the Strategic Hamlet Program of 1962?
options: A counterinsurgency program resettling villagers in fortified hamlets
A program to build dams on the Mekong
An aid program for rice farmers in the north
questions.explain: It was part of Diem's counterinsurgency effort, along with land reform and resettlement.

questions.q: What caused unrest and hurt Diem's support with the United States in 1963?
options: His plan to unify with the north
His repression of Buddhists and favoritism to Catholics
questions.explain: The Buddhist crisis weakened his support in the army and damaged relations with Washington.

questions.q: Who was removed as Cambodia's leader on March 18, 1970, in a vote of the National Assembly?
questions.explain: Prime Minister Lon Nol took power, with Cheng Heng as formal head of state, and Sihanouk, in exile in Beijing, called for an uprising and allied with the Khmer Rouge and North Vietnam.

questions.q: What was the aim of the 1970 allied operations in eastern Cambodia?
options: To destroy North Vietnamese and Viet Cong base areas near the border
To open a route to Thailand
questions.explain: U.S. forces operated there from May 1 to June 30, 1970. The campaign captured large amounts of supplies.

questions.q: What was the Ho Chi Minh Trail?
options: A road in Hanoi named for Ho Chi Minh
A railroad from China to Saigon
A river route through the Mekong Delta
A network of roads and paths through Laos and Cambodia that supplied communist forces
questions.explain: Construction began after the invasion of Laos in July 1959, and the trail was used until 1975.

questions.q: Which U.S. air campaign, begun in December 1964, bombed targets in Laos?
questions.explain: U.S. bombing included Barrel Roll, Steel Tiger, Tiger Hound and Commando Hunt.

questions.q: Which of these did North Vietnamese engineers build along the Ho Chi Minh Trail in the late 1960s?
options: A deep-water port at Da Nang
questions.explain: North Vietnamese engineers built a fuel pipeline through the Mu Gia Pass to support trucks and troops moving south.

questions.q: Which future senator was held as a prisoner at Hoa Lo Prison, the "Hanoi Hilton"?
questions.explain: McCain was among notable inmates, as were Jeremiah Denton, James Stockdale and Everett Alvarez Jr.

questions.q: Who was held for over eight years in North Vietnamese prisons, one of the longest-held American POWs?
questions.explain: Alvarez, held for more than eight years, was among prominent inmates at Hoa Lo.

questions.q: What was Operation Ranch Hand, which ran from 1962 to 1971?
options: A program to resettle Vietnamese farmers
A program that sprayed herbicides including Agent Orange in Vietnam
A rescue mission for downed pilots
questions.explain: Nearly 20 million gallons were sprayed to strip vegetation that hid enemy forces and to destroy crops.

questions.q: What did a 1984 class-action settlement require chemical companies to do about Agent Orange?
questions.explain: Seven chemical companies agreed in 1984 to a $180 million settlement fund for U.S. veterans and their families.

questions.q: What did President Johnson do during the Tonkin Gulf incident on August 4, 1964, after the reported second attack?
options: Announced retaliatory strikes on North Vietnam
Sent a message to Moscow offering talks
questions.explain: Johnson announced retaliatory strikes the same day and sent the resolution to the Senate on August 5.

questions.q: In what year was the repeal of the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution signed into law?
questions.explain: The Senate voted to repeal the resolution in June 1970, and Nixon signed the repeal in January 1971, but funding for the war continued until U.S. forces withdrew in March 1973.

questions.q: About how many United Nations Command casualties did the U.S. Army history count in the Korean War?
options: More than 5 million, including about 950,000 dead
questions.explain: The Army history says United Nations forces suffered over 559,000 casualties during the war, including approximately 94,000 dead.

questions.q: Roughly how many enemy casualties, including prisoners, did the Army history estimate in Korea?
options: About 150,000, of whom about 90,000 were Chinese
About 5 million, of whom about 2 million were Chinese and Korean
About 600,000, of whom about 100,000 were Chinese
More than 1.5 million, of whom about 900,000 were Chinese
questions.explain: The Army history counts enemy casualties above 1,500,000, about 900,000 of them Chinese.

questions.q: How many Army National Guard divisions were mobilized for the Korean War?
questions.explain: The Army history notes that eight Army National Guard divisions were mobilized during the war.

questions.q: Which Army unit arrived in Korea from Okinawa in late July 1950 to reinforce the defense of the south?
questions.explain: Two battalions of the 29th Infantry arrived from Okinawa in late July 1950 and were sent into the line near Chinju almost at once.

questions.q: Which Marine unit was among the first reinforcements for the Pusan Perimeter in the summer of 1950?
questions.explain: Reinforcements included the 5th RCT from Hawaii, the 2nd Infantry Division, the 1st Provisional Marine Brigade and a British brigade.

questions.q: What did Truman authorize on June 30, 1950, when he expanded MacArthur's authority in Korea?
options: A nuclear attack on North Korea
A draft of all men under 30
Use of Army ground forces beyond protecting Pusan
questions.explain: A June 29 directive let MacArthur use Army troops to hold a port and air base near Pusan. On June 30 Truman approved sending a regiment and then two divisions from Japan into combat.

questions.q: Which U.S. division was badly hurt at Kunu-ri in late November 1950 while covering the retreat?
questions.explain: The 2nd Division suffered heavily at Kunu-ri in late November 1950 after the Chinese offensive that began on November 25.

questions.q: Which North Korean capital was abandoned by U.N. forces on December 5, 1950?
questions.explain: U.N. forces abandoned Pyongyang as Chinese forces pushed south after the November attacks.

questions.q: When did General Ridgway's counteroffensive begin in 1951, with operations including Thunderbolt and Killer?
questions.explain: Ridgway's counteroffensive began on January 25, 1951, and Seoul was liberated again by mid-March.

questions.q: About how far above the 38th parallel was Line KANSAS, which UN forces reached in spring 1951?
questions.explain: After Seoul was retaken, UN forces advanced to Line KANSAS, which ran from a few miles to about 10 miles above the 38th parallel across most of its length, then pushed toward the Iron Triangle.

questions.q: What order did Ridgway give Van Fleet on November 12, 1951, as the war settled into a stalemate?
options: To attack across the Yalu River
questions.explain: The order reflected the shift to a defensive posture while armistice talks continued.

questions.q: Which Chinese commander led the Chinese People's Volunteer Army in Korea?
questions.explain: Peng Dehuai commanded the Chinese People's Volunteer Army in Korea and signed the 1953 armistice for the Chinese side.

questions.q: About how tall is each of the 19 stainless steel statues of the patrol at the Korean War Veterans Memorial?
options: About seven and a half feet
questions.explain: Each figure stands between 7 feet 3 inches and 7 feet 6 inches, so they appear larger than life.

questions.q: What kind of stone is the Mural Wall of the Korean War Veterans Memorial made of?
questions.explain: The Mural Wall is black granite from California, sandblasted with images of service members.

questions.q: About how large is the site of the Korean War Veterans Memorial?
questions.explain: The Korean War Veterans Memorial covers about 2.2 acres in West Potomac Park. It was dedicated in 1995 and features 19 statues of soldiers on patrol.

questions.q: Which corps, led by the 7th Infantry Division, reached the Yalu River at Hyesanjin on November 21, 1950?
questions.explain: X Corps, led by the 7th Division's 17th Infantry, reached the Yalu River at Hyesanjin on November 21, 1950.

questions.q: Which Soviet leader died in March 1953, an event many historians say eased the way toward the Korean armistice?
questions.explain: Stalin died on March 5, 1953. His successors were more willing to end the war, and the armistice followed in July.

questions.q: What did the Truman administration authorize for UN forces on September 27, 1950?
options: Military operations north of the 38th parallel
questions.explain: Truman authorized MacArthur to send his forces north of the 38th parallel on September 27, and the UN General Assembly backed the move in early October.

questions.q: Which words are inlaid in silver letters on the wall opposite the casualty curb at the Korean War Veterans Memorial?
questions.explain: The National Park Service says the inscription Freedom Is Not Free is inlaid in silver letters on the wall opposite the casualty curb.

questions.q: How many linden trees surround the Pool of Remembrance at the Korean War Veterans Memorial?
questions.explain: The National Park Service says the 128-foot circular pool is surrounded by 40 linden trees, with benches set beneath them.

questions.q: According to the National Park Service, about how many photographs of service members does the Mural Wall display?
questions.explain: The National Park Service says the Mural Wall displays more than 2,400 photographs of Korean War service members.
